speaker: Romeo Montague
text: Hey, Juliet. Sorry, give me one second, I'm just getting my screen up.

speaker: Juliet Capulet
text: No rush. How's your day?

speaker: Romeo Montague
text: Good, actually. I've been playing with the queue all morning. But you first. How was Ducal?

speaker: Juliet Capulet
text: Really good. Paris was great, very clear about what he needs. He asked for three things.

speaker: Romeo Montague
text: Okay, go.

speaker: Juliet Capulet
text: One, inspections that sync on their own when the tablet comes back online. Their yards have basically no signal past the first few rows of trailers. Two, a signed PDF for every inspection, because their auditors need a signed report within twenty-four hours. And three, export into their freight system, by site. They've got thirty sites.

speaker: Romeo Montague
text: Okay. So the first one is literally the queue.

speaker: Juliet Capulet
text: That's what I was hoping you'd say.

speaker: Romeo Montague
text: The PDF is all you, that's Balcony. And export by site, um, that's new. That's not this week.

speaker: Juliet Capulet
text: No, agreed. I told him I'd be straight with him on timing. Oh, and he asked whether Ducal would see your routing data. I said no, only what Ducal sends.

speaker: Romeo Montague
text: Good. Yes. That's right. Okay, can I show you the thing?

speaker: Juliet Capulet
text: Please.

speaker: Romeo Montague
text: So this is the prototype on a test tablet. At about two I turned off the wifi and just started making inspections. Fake ones. Dock four, dock seven, a very damaged imaginary trailer.

speaker: Juliet Capulet
text: Poor trailer.

speaker: Romeo Montague
text: It's had a hard day. So you can see here, twelve inspections queued. That's an hour offline. Nothing crashed, nothing got lost. Now watch. I'm turning the wifi back on.

speaker: Juliet Capulet
text: Okay...

speaker: Romeo Montague
text: And there it goes. Eleven, eight, four... zero. All twelve sent, in order, and they're showing up on the Mesh Routing side. Same timestamps they were signed with, not the time they arrived.

speaker: Juliet Capulet
text: Oh, that's important. The auditors care about when it was signed.

speaker: Romeo Montague
text: Exactly. That was the whole point of keeping the signed time on the record.

speaker: Juliet Capulet
text: That's really nice, Romeo. Tybalt said this morning he's satisfied if it survives a week of airplane mode.

speaker: Romeo Montague
text: Ha. Okay. One hour down, a hundred and sixty-seven to go.

speaker: Juliet Capulet
text: So, the thing I really want to settle today. Field versioning. It's the one open question left from Monday, and I've got an empty owner line in the spec staring at me.

speaker: Romeo Montague
text: Yeah. I've been thinking about it. Can I propose something?

speaker: Juliet Capulet
text: Go for it.

speaker: Romeo Montague
text: So there are really two layers. There's the inspection record itself. Site, inspector, photos, findings, signed time. That's yours, that's what Balcony knows about. And then there's the envelope around it, the routing stuff, where it's going, delivery, retries. That's ours.

speaker: Juliet Capulet
text: So Capulet owns the inspection record schema, Montague owns the routing envelope.

speaker: Romeo Montague
text: Right. But, and here's the part I care about, any change to either one needs both of us to approve it. Because if you rename a field, my side breaks, and if I change the envelope, your side breaks.

speaker: Juliet Capulet
text: I like that. Each side owns its part, nobody changes anything alone.

speaker: Romeo Montague
text: Yeah.

speaker: Juliet Capulet
text: Okay. Decided. I'll write it into the spec tonight. How do we know which version an event is on, though?

speaker: Romeo Montague
text: I'll add a schema version number to every event. So if we ever change something, an old tablet sending old events doesn't confuse anybody. The receiver just reads the number.

speaker: Juliet Capulet
text: Perfect. Okay, last thing. Friday's demo. What do we show Paris?

speaker: Romeo Montague
text: I think exactly what I just showed you. An inspection done offline, then the tablet reconnects and it syncs.

speaker: Juliet Capulet
text: And then I show the signed PDF for that same inspection. So he sees his first two asks, start to finish.

speaker: Romeo Montague
text: Love that. And we just say export by site is coming, honestly.

speaker: Juliet Capulet
text: Honestly. Okay. I think we're in good shape. Thanks, Romeo.

speaker: Romeo Montague
text: Thank you. Say hi to Tybalt. Tell him the clock's running.
